title: Jesus / Son Research Index
purpose: Provide one durable entry point for the project's Jesus/Son research so prison, Passion, Thomas, Lamb/Lion, death/return, Door/Cornerstone and Father/Son material is discoverable as one connected field rather than scattered files.

entry_sequence.use: Identity boundary and year-by-year Son timeline.
Long developmental genealogy and pre-Christian/Christian precursor strata.
Claim-by-claim source status and unresolved attribution questions.
Yahya Hassan/inmate Jesus-Lamb recognition sequence with evidence boundary.
Full-life Jesus/Son comparison from early care and healing through prison, recognition, crucifixion imagery, Thomas, grain, cornerstone, Door and Father relation.
Later Tim/Father relation and Godhood question kept separate from the Son's historical biography.

high_value_questions: What is the earliest recoverable instance of someone else calling the Son Jesus?
Can the exact Yahya Hassan wording and prison location/date be independently corroborated?
What is the earliest dated instance of the Son himself saying 'I am Jesus Christ' or asking to be crucified?
Does the original Josh Moon recording survive, and what is the exact wording and date?
When does the grain-of-wheat-in-the-heart motif first appear relative to the meme death?
When does Thomas/Didymus/Twin first become attached to the Son?
When does rejected-stone/cornerstone language first appear?
When does the Son first become Door/Vessel rather than merely a person?
Which 2016 statements are primary-authenticated and which are only media-attributed?
How much of the Passion comparison existed before 2019, and how much is retrospective synthesis?
Which parallels are genuinely unusual because they precede the later theology?
Which apparent parallels disappear once timeline and source provenance are checked?
interpretive_rule: The strongest project argument is chronological and relational: identify what existed before later interpretation, then show how later events reorganized earlier material. Do not convert resemblance into proof of supernatural identity.
public_reader_summary: The project studies an accumulating Jesus/Son pattern: care and outsider affinity, institutional conflict, imprisonment and scripture, claimed external Jesus/Lamb recognition, later explicit Jesus/crucifixion self-language, public ridicule and rejection, meme-death/burial, Thomas/Twin and grain/seed interpretation, and eventual Door/Cornerstone/Father-Son architecture. Each link carries its own source status and mismatches.
